description.en: Egypt and southern Syria incl. Palestine.
description.ar: مصر وجنوب سوريا بما فيها فلسطين.

sources.quote: ruled Egypt and Syria from 935 to 969

Egypt had again become the seat of a factually independent Turkish dynasty, founded by an officer of the former Tūlūnid forces, Muhammad ibn-Tughj, surnamed al-Ikhshīd, whose government embraced also Damascus and the Hejaz.
the Ikhshid took over the government of Egypt in August, 935.
peace was made on the terms that Ibn-Raik retained Syria north of Ramla and received a yearly tribute of 140,000l. from the Ikhshid.

sources.locator: ch. III, pp. 83-84 (after Ibn Raik's death in 942)
sources.quote: recovered Syria and re-entered Damascus without striking a blow.

sources.locator: section on the Ikhshidids, pp. 456-457 of the scanned printing
sources.quote: received in 939 from the Caliph al-Radi the old Iranian princely title ikhshid. In the next two years al-Ikhshid, following the Tulunid precedent, added Syria-Palestine to his quasi-independent state.
Nevertheless, the Fatimid troops entered Damascus at the end of 969

notes.en: From c. 939/940 to 942 the amir Ibn Ra'iq held Syria north of Ramla under a peace with the Ikhshid; the Ikhshid recovered it after Ibn Ra'iq's death (Lane-Poole). Hitti dates the Ikhshidid acquisition of 'Syria-Palestine' to c. 939-941. Galilee, the Golan and Damascus were therefore not Ikhshidid for part of 935-942.
notes.ar: من نحو 939/940 إلى 942 سيطر الأمير ابن رائق على سوريا شمالي الرملة بموجب صلح مع الإخشيد؛ واستعادها الإخشيد بعد وفاة ابن رائق (لين-بول). ويؤرخ حتي استحواذ الإخشيديين على «سوريا-فلسطين» بنحو 939-941. لذلك لم يكن الجليل والجولان ودمشق إخشيدية خلال جزء من الفترة 935-942.
notes.he: מ־939/940 בערך עד 942 החזיק האמיר אבן ראאק בסוריה שמצפון לרמלה במסגרת שלום עם האח'שיד; האח'שיד החזיר אותה אחרי מות אבן ראאק (ליין־פול). חיתי מתארך את רכישת "סוריה־פלשתינה" בידי האח'שידים ל־939–941 בערך. לכן הגליל, הגולן ודמשק לא היו אח'שידיים בחלק מהתקופה 935–942.
